answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake bond before it can earn, like a pearl forming layer by layer around a real deposit. A fake army must fund every copy, so the cost ripples outward with each new identity instead of staying flat. Misbehavior slashes the bond, and honest work slowly grows it into a jade-grade reputation that cannot be bought instantly, making mass fakery expensive and slow.
